title: Pixel Invisible: online hide and seek where you paint your own 32×32 body to blend into AI-generated pixel-art stages (Android out now, iOS in review)
author: nakasy
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev! I just released Pixel Invisible on Android. The iOS version is in App Store review right now and should be out soon.



\*\*The game\*\*



\- Hiders are tanuki who mix RGB colors and paint their own 32×32 body to blend into furniture and floors. You can also tap the scene with an eyedropper to pick up colors.

\- The seeker, the "Agent Tanuki", fires a cork gun at suspicious spots. Ammo is limited.

\- 2–10 players online (random matchmaking with role-based ratings, or a private room with a 5-letter code), or solo practice against bots.

\- 10 stages: mansion, warehouse, forest, school, shopping street, factory, aquarium, amusement park, haunted house and spaceship.



\*\*How AI fits in\*\*



All the art started as AI-generated images: the characters, 120 furniture pieces and props, floor and wall textures, icons, the logo and the UI panels. The raw images couldn't go straight into the game, because the camouflage only works if the background and the paintable body use exactly the same colors. So I built an import tool that:



\- slices the sprite sheets into single assets and fits the characters to a 32×32 grid with a shared foot position

\- removes leftover color on transparent edges and makes alpha strictly on/off

\- maps everything to a 248-color palette (32 base colors plus 216 RGB colors at 6 steps per channel). Players mix colors from the same palette.

\- makes 6 color variations of each prop from one generated image



I also generated whole stage illustrations, but used them only as design references. The playable maps are built from tiles and props so what you see always matches where you can walk.



An automated check tests every walkable position, 1 px at a time, in all 4 poses. It fails if the background under the body has 2 colors or fewer, so you can never hide by filling your body with one flat color. Blank surfaces get small texture patterns when the maps are built.



\*\*Tech\*\*



Unity. Matches are peer-to-peer, with Firebase handling accounts, rooms and connection setup. If the host leaves, another player takes over and the match keeps going.



Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cad.pixel](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cad.pixel)

iOS: in review



I'd love feedback, especially on whether the art reads well at this size. Happy to answer questions about the pipeline!
